occurrence.label: Hyperscaler AI capex supercycle

title: AI infrastructure buildout: the un-crowded links
thesis: Hyperscaler AI capex is a multi-year physical buildout whose downstream links (chips, memory) are fully discovered while upstream links (power equipment, grid, cooling, generation) remain under-owned relative to their exposure. The chain, not the headline, is the opportunity.
why_now: 2025-2026 hyperscaler capex guidance kept rising while power availability, not chip supply, became the stated binding constraint in multiple earnings calls and utility interconnection queues.
retail_gap: Retail owns the story at the GPU/memory layer. Transformer lead times, switchgear backlogs, and grid capex inflection are visible in primary sources but barely present in retail attention data.

unmappedness.rationale: The first 4-5 links are saturated narrative; links 9-12 (cooling, power, grid, generation) are mapped by sell-side but thinly held and rarely discussed as a chain.

evidence.claim: Hyperscalers guided aggregate 2026 AI/data-center capex further up in mid-2026 earnings calls; buildout demand is anchored by disclosed plans, not sentiment.
Power availability and interconnection timelines are repeatedly named by operators as the binding constraint on new data-center capacity.
evidence.source_name: utility and data-center operator commentary, interconnection queue reporting

evidence.claim: GE Vernova disclosed a total company backlog above $100B (largest power-equipment backlog ever reported), $38.6B of it in equipment; US standard power-transformer lead times average ~128 weeks and generator step-up units ~144 weeks, with a mid-2026 GSU order quoted for 2029 delivery.
evidence.source_name: GE Vernova Q1 FY2026 8-K (filed 2026-04-22); PowerMag / HVDC America / ChargedUpPro transformer-market reporting

evidence.claim: 30-50% of planned data-center sites are at risk of delay or cancellation on transformer and switchgear shortages against >$750B of 2026 hyperscaler capex; Microsoft/Constellation are restarting Three Mile Island Unit 1 (835MW, target 2028) and Amazon/Talen are taking up to 1,920MW from Susquehanna as near-term power fixes while SMRs remain a 2030s solution (only 9.8GW committed nuclear capacity, 80.4% not yet in commercial operation as of July 2026).
evidence.source_name: ChargedUpPro / Axis Intelligence / Layer3Labs nuclear-for-AI reporting
